one_liner: Senior Executive running CISA Central, the agency's 24/7 watch-and-warning hub that coordinates threat information and incident response for cyber and physical infrastructure.
fit_summary: This SES job requires executive leadership of people, budgets, acquisition and human capital programs at scale, plus cyber operations. Daniel's exercise and emergency planning work touches the mission, but his resume shows no executive or cyber experience, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include 'public'), so you do not need federal status, and veterans' preference does not apply to SES.
You must show all five Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) and both Technical Qualifications (TQs) inside a resume of no more than 2 pages. Separate narratives are not accepted.
You must be able to obtain a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance, pass a drug test, and file an OGE-278 financial disclosure.
Before appointment, OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB) must certify the selectee's executive qualifications.
U.S. citizenship and Selective Service registration (if applicable) are required. Education cannot be substituted for experience.
strategy: Skip this one: this SES job requires executive leadership of people, budgets, acquisition and human capital programs at scale, plus cyber operations, and his resume shows no executive or cyber experience.
Put the effort into GS-9 to GS-12 CISA or FEMA roles in operations or preparedness, where his exercise and emergency management work fits.
resume_bullets: Led a Simulation Cell unit at FEMA full-scale exercises two years in a row.
Facilitated full-scale and tabletop exercises for federal, state and private-sector clients (2022–2024).
interview_questions: Describe a time you led a team through change and held people accountable for results.
How have you formulated or justified a multi-year budget or acquisition strategy?
How would you keep situational awareness and coordination going across CISA, DHS components, and private-sector partners during a major incident?
Tell us about building trust with a skeptical senior official or stakeholder group.
watch_outs: This is an SES executive role, and your known experience likely falls well short of the ECQ and TQ requirements.
It requires SCI clearance eligibility and may be designated essential personnel (reporting during closures and continuity events).
The posting says Washington, DC, but the duty location is Arlington, VA.
